rawInner: Prevent layout shifts with aspect ratio Set `aspect-ratio` so nearby content does not jump while an image loads.
Balance heading text for easier reading Use `text-balance` for headings and `text-pretty` for body copy.
Align numbers with tabular-nums Use `tabular-nums` to align numbers in tables and data-heavy UI.
Use 44px touch targets for accessibility Give buttons and controls a touch target of at least 44 by 44px.
Match border radius on nested elements Set the nested element's radius to the parent's radius minus its padding. Formula: `inner radius = outer radius - padding`
Add scale feedback to pressed buttons Add subtle press feedback with `:active` and a scale near 0.96.
Animate popovers from their trigger Animate each popover from the control that opened it.
Group content with spacing, not dividers Use spacing to group related content before adding divider lines.
Preview the next item in scroll lists Show 16 to 32px of the next item to make horizontal scrolling clear.
Use neutral borders around images Use a thin neutral outline instead of a tinted ring.
Truncate long titles in small spaces Use `line-clamp` or `truncate` when space is tight.
Improve contrast for muted text Give muted text enough color contrast to stay easy to read.
Avoid scale-zero entrance animations Start entrance animations near 95% size instead of scaling up from zero.
Match loading skeletons to real content Match loading skeletons to the content they replace, and skip spinners when possible.
Limit each view to one accent color Use one accent per view. Keep secondary actions neutral.
Keep body text lines easy to read Keep text lines between 60 and 75 characters for easier reading.
Use shadows to show visual depth Use shadows to show depth. Use borders to show structure.
Add visible keyboard focus rings Use `:focus-visible` to keep keyboard focus clear and visible.
Show form errors next to each field Put each validation error directly below its field.
Add visible labels to every form field Use a visible label. Do not use placeholder text as the only label.
Give empty states one clear action Give an empty state one clear action, not just an explanation.
Use sentence case for UI labels Write labels in sentence case, not all caps.
Never use color alone for status Add text or an icon so status is never shown by color alone.
Use ease-out for entrance animations Use `ease-out` for entrances. `ease-in` feels slow when something opens.
Align icons by eye for better balance Nudge icons when geometric centering does not look visually balanced.
Match icon stroke weight to text Use a 2px stroke beside semibold text and a 1.5px stroke beside regular text.
Use outline icons for default states Use outline icons by default. Use a fill for the active state.
Avoid glow effects on primary buttons Avoid glow effects on primary buttons; use contrast and spacing instead.
Animate icon state changes smoothly Cross-fade changing icons with opacity, scale, and blur for smoother feedback.
Add space between nearby controls Leave about 12px between nearby bordered controls.
Keep full-width buttons inside page margins Keep full-width buttons inside the page margins, not edge to edge.
Use tighter line height for headings Use a line height near 1.1 for short headings.
Adjust letter spacing for large text Large display text often needs slightly tighter letter spacing.
Confirm destructive actions before they run Ask for confirmation before deleting data or taking an irreversible action.
Fade the edges of scrollable lists Use a `mask-image` fade to show where a scrollable list continues.
Stagger hero animations on first load Stagger hero animations by about 100ms on first load, not during routine interactions.
Keep exit animations short and subtle Keep exit animations short with a small `translateY` movement.
Show nearby tooltips faster Show nearby tooltips faster after the first tooltip opens.
Use interruptible CSS transitions Use CSS transitions for interactive open and close states.
Avoid repeated animations in routine UI Animate first-load entrances, but keep repeated actions like tab switches instant.
Use ease-out instead of springs for feedback Use `ease-out` for toggles and toasts because springs can wobble.
Fade menus out when they close Close menus with a short fade. Do not move them far off screen.
Reserve brand colors for links and actions Keep headings neutral. Use the brand color for links and actions.
Use solid modal backdrops instead of blur Use a solid modal backdrop instead of blur to avoid expensive full-screen rendering.
Fade overflowing text instead of clipping it Fade long labels instead of cutting them off with a hard ellipsis.
Use matching enter and exit animations Use matching enter and exit animations so a surface feels connected.
Soften label changes with a short blur Add a short blur when labels change to avoid a distracting visual flash.
